conceptCapsule.title: Kinematic String Constraints & Dynamics of Pulley Systems
conceptCapsule.summary: 1. String Constraint Relations: For inextensible strings over ideal pulleys, the total length is invariant ($\sum l_i = \text{const}$). Differentiating yields velocity and acceleration constraints: $\sum \vec{T}_i \cdot \vec{v}_i = 0$ and $\sum \vec{T}_i \cdot \vec{a}_i = 0$ (Virtual Work Method). 2. Movable Pulley Mechanical Advantage: If a block is supported by a 2-strand movable pulley, $a_{\text{block}} = \frac{a_{\text{free\_end}}}{2}$ and effective upward tension is $2T$. 3. Center of Mass Acceleration: In a two-body Atwood machine, $a = \frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}g$, with center-of-mass downward acceleration $a_{\text{cm}} = \left(\frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}\right)^2 g$.
conceptCapsule.keyFormula: $$\sum \vec{T}_i \cdot \vec{a}_i = 0, \quad a_{\text{movable}} = \frac{a_{\text{table}}}{2}, \quad a_{\text{cm}} = \left(\frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}\right)^2 g, \quad v_{\text{block}} = \frac{u}{\cos\theta}$$
conceptCapsule.examTrap: When a string pulled with speed $u$ at an angle $	heta$ to the horizontal pulls a block along a floor, the block velocity is $v = \frac{u}{\cos\theta}$ (NOT $u\cos\theta$). The physical constraint is that the rate of shortening of the string equals $u$, which gives $v\cos\theta = u$.

questions.statement: In a system with a movable pulley $P_1$ carrying mass $m_1 = 4\text{ kg}$ and a fixed pulley $P_2$, a single light string connects mass $m_2 = 1\text{ kg}$ on a smooth table to $m_1$ via $P_1$. If the table block moves with acceleration $a_2$, the acceleration $a_1$ of the hanging movable pulley block is:
questions.solution:
Length of string $l = x_2 + 2y_1 + \text{constant}$. Differentiating twice with respect to time yields $\ddot{x}_2 + 2\ddot{y}_1 = 0 \implies a_1 = \frac{a_2}{2}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: In the system of Q1, the acceleration $a_1$ of the hanging mass $m_1$ is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
1. For $m_2$: $T = m_2 a_2 = m_2(2a_1) = 2m_2 a_1$.
2. For $m_1$: $m_1 g - 2T = m_1 a_1 \implies m_1 g - 4m_2 a_1 = m_1 a_1$.
3. $a_1 = \frac{m_1 g}{m_1 + 4m_2} = \frac{4 \times 10}{4 + 4(1)} = \frac{40}{8} = 5.0\text{ m/s}^2$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: In an Atwood machine with masses $m_1 = 6\text{ kg}$ and $m_2 = 4\text{ kg}$, the acceleration of the center of mass of the two-mass system ($a_{\text{cm}}$) is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
1. Individual acceleration $a = \frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}g = \frac{2}{10}(10) = 2.0\text{ m/s}^2$.
2. $a_{\text{cm}} = \left(\frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}\right)a = \left(\frac{2}{10}\right)(2.0) = 0.4\text{ m/s}^2\text{ (downward)}$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m_1$ on a horizontal table is pulled by a string passing over a fixed pulley at height $h$. When the string makes an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal and the free end is pulled with constant speed $u$, the speed of block $m_1$ along the table is:
questions.solution:
Position constraint: $x^2 + h^2 = l^2 \implies 2x\frac{dx}{dt} = 2l\frac{dl}{dt} \implies x v = l u \implies v = u\frac{l}{x} = \frac{u}{\cos\theta}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: In a modified Atwood machine, a hanging mass $m_1 = 2\text{ kg}$ pulls two masses $m_2 = 3\text{ kg}$ and $m_3 = 5\text{ kg}$ tied together by a string on a frictionless table. The tension in the string between $m_2$ and $m_3$ is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
1. Acceleration $a = \frac{m_1 g}{m_1 + m_2 + m_3} = \frac{20}{10} = 2.0\text{ m/s}^2$.
2. Tension $T_{23}$ pulls $m_3$: $T_{23} = m_3 a = 5 \times 2.0 = 10\text{ N}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A system consists of three blocks $A, B,$ and $C$ of masses $m_A = 1\text{ kg}$, $m_B = 2\text{ kg}$, and $m_C = 3\text{ kg}$ connected vertically by strings in a single line. If pulled upward with an acceleration $a = 2\text{ m/s}^2$, the tension in the string connecting $A$ and $B$ (where $A$ is the top block) is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
Tension $T_{AB}$ supports $(m_B + m_C) = 5\text{ kg}$: $$T_{AB} = (m_B + m_C)(g + a) = 5(10 + 2) = 60\text{ N}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A block $A$ of mass $M$ slides on a frictionless horizontal floor. A light string attached to $A$ passes over a smooth pulley and holds a hanging block $B$ of mass $m$. The force exerted by the pulley clamp on the table corner is:
questions.solution:
The two string segments pull horizontally and vertically at $90^\circ$ on the corner pulley: $$F_{\text{pulley}} = \sqrt{T^2 + T^2} = \sqrt{2}T$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: Two masses $m_1 = 3\text{ kg}$ and $m_2 = 1\text{ kg}$ are connected by a light string over a smooth pulley. Mass $m_1$ is placed on a smooth incline of angle $	heta = 30^\circ$, while $m_2$ hangs vertically. The acceleration of mass $m_1$ down the incline is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
1. Driving force: $F_{\text{net}} = m_1 g\sin 30^\circ - m_2 g = 15 - 10 = 5\text{ N}$.
2. Total mass: $M = 3 + 1 = 4\text{ kg}$.
3. $a = \frac{5}{4} = 1.25\text{ m/s}^2$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: In a virtual work constraint problem, if $\sum \vec{T}_i \cdot \vec{a}_i = 0$ is applied to a connected pulley system, the underlying physical assumption is that:

options.text: Pulleys are frictionless but have finite rotational inertia
Strings are massless, inextensible, and pulleys are ideal
The acceleration of all masses is identical
Mechanical energy is dissipated as heat

questions.solution:
The relation $\sum \vec{T}_i \cdot \vec{a}_i = 0$ is valid when internal tension does zero net work, which requires massless, inextensible strings and frictionless, massless pulleys.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m$ is suspended by a string wrapped around two identical fixed pulleys and one movable pulley. If the free end of the string is pulled down with acceleration $a_0$, the upward acceleration of mass $m$ is:
questions.solution:
Since mass $m$ is supported by two strands of string from the movable pulley, $2y_m = x_0 \implies a_m = \frac{a_0}{2}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A monkey of mass $m = 30\text{ kg}$ climbs up a light rope attached to a counterweight block of mass $M = 30\text{ kg}$ over a smooth fixed pulley. If the monkey accelerates up the rope at $2\text{ m/s}^2$ relative to the rope, the acceleration of the block $M$ relative to the ground is:
questions.solution:
1. For counterweight $M$: $T - Mg = Ma_M$.
2. For monkey $m$: $T - mg = m(a_{\text{rel}} - a_M)$.
3. Equating tensions: $a_M + g = (a_{\text{rel}} - a_M) + g \implies 2a_M = 2 \implies a_M = 1.0\text{ m/s}^2\text{ (upward)}$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: Two blocks of masses $m_1 = 2\text{ kg}$ and $m_2 = 3\text{ kg}$ are connected by a spring of stiffness $k = 100\text{ N/m}$ on a frictionless horizontal plane. If a constant force $F = 20\text{ N}$ pulls $m_2$ horizontally, the maximum extension of the spring from its natural length is:
questions.solution:
$$x_{\max} = \frac{2 m_1 F}{k(m_1 + m_2)} = \frac{2(2)(20)}{100(2 + 3)} = \frac{80}{500} = 0.16\text{ m}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A double pulley system has a fixed pulley and a movable pulley. Mass $m_1 = 4\text{ kg}$ hangs from the movable pulley, while mass $m_2 = 1\text{ kg}$ hangs from the free end of the string. The tension in the string is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
1. Constraint: $a_2 = 2a_1$.
2. $m_1 g - 2T = m_1 a_1 \implies 40 - 2T = 4a_1$.
3. $T - m_2 g = m_2(2a_1) \implies a_1 = \frac{T - 10}{2}$.
4. $40 - 2T = 2T - 20 \implies 4T = 64 \implies T = 16.0\text{ N}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: In Q13, the downward acceleration of the hanging mass $m_1$ attached to the movable pulley is:
questions.solution:
$$a_1 = \frac{m_1 - 2m_2}{m_1 + 4m_2}g = \frac{4 - 2(1)}{4 + 4(1)}(10) = \frac{2}{8}(10) = 2.0\text{ m/s}^2$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m_1 = 5\text{ kg}$ is on a smooth horizontal table. It is connected by a string passing over a smooth pulley to a movable pulley of mass $m_p = 0$. The movable pulley supports two hanging masses $m_2 = 2\text{ kg}$ and $m_3 = 3\text{ kg}$. The tension in the string supporting $m_1$ is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
1. Effective mass of hanging Atwood branch: $m_{\text{eff}} = \frac{4 m_2 m_3}{m_2 + m_3} = \frac{4(2)(3)}{5} = 4.8\text{ kg}$.
2. Tension: $T = \frac{m_1 m_{\text{eff}} g}{m_1 + m_{\text{eff}}} = \frac{5(4.8)(10)}{5 + 4.8} = \frac{240}{9.8} \approx 28.2\text{ N}$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $M = 10\text{ kg}$ is resting on a frictionless horizontal plane. A light string attached to $M$ passes over a frictionless pulley and carries a block of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$. If the system is released from rest, the distance traveled by block $M$ in $t = 2\text{ seconds}$ is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
1. $a = \frac{mg}{M + m} = \frac{20}{12} = \frac{5}{3}\text{ m/s}^2$.
2. Distance in $2\text{ s}$: $s = \frac{1}{2}at^2 = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)(4) = \frac{10}{3} \approx 3.33\text{ m}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: In a system of connected masses on a smooth wedge of inclination $	heta = 45^\circ$, mass $m_1 = 4\text{ kg}$ on the incline is connected via a light string over the apex pulley to a hanging mass $m_2 = 4\text{ kg}$. The tension in the connecting string is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, $\sqrt{2} \approx 1.414$)
questions.solution:
1. $F_{\text{net}} = 40 - 40\sin 45^\circ = 11.72\text{ N} \implies a = \frac{11.72}{8} = 1.465\text{ m/s}^2$.
2. Tension: $T = 4(10 - 1.465) = 4(8.535) \approx 34.1\text{ N}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: Three masses $m_1 = 2\text{ kg}$, $m_2 = 3\text{ kg}$, and $m_3 = 5\text{ kg}$ are connected by strings as an Atwood machine where $m_1$ and $m_2$ hang together on one side and $m_3$ hangs on the other. The tension in the string connecting $m_1$ and $m_2$ is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
Since $(m_1 + m_2) = m_3 = 5\text{ kg}$, the system has zero acceleration ($a = 0$). FBD of $m_1$: $$T_{12} = m_1 g = 2 \times 10 = 20\text{ N}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A ring of mass $m$ slides along a smooth fixed vertical rod. It is connected by a string passing over a smooth pulley at distance $d$ from the rod to a hanging mass $M$. When the string makes an angle $	heta$ with the vertical, the ring is in static equilibrium if:
questions.solution:
Tension in string is $T = Mg$. Vertical equilibrium of the ring: $$T\cos\theta = mg \implies (Mg)\cos\theta = mg \implies \cos\theta = \frac{m}{M}$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: Two particles of masses $m$ and $2m$ are connected by a light string passing over a frictionless pulley. If the system is initially held at rest and then released, the velocity of the center of mass after time $t$ is:
questions.solution:
1. Acceleration $a = \frac{2m - m}{3m}g = \frac{g}{3}$.
2. $a_{\text{cm}} = \left(\frac{2m - m}{3m}\right)a = \frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{g}{3}\right) = \frac{g}{9}\text{ (downward)}$.
3. Velocity $v_{\text{cm}} = a_{\text{cm}} t = \frac{gt}{9}\text{ (downward)}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.
